title: Headless execution: Chrome and Firefox without a UI

videos.script: Your tests have been running without a window since lesson 1. This lesson is about what that means. {{headless}} A headless browser still parses the page, runs its scripts, lays it out and paints it. It just paints into memory, with no screen to show it on. {{pipeline}} Chromium has two headless modes, and Playwright ships both. A small shell, used by default, and the full browser with its window switched off. {{two}} You ask each one its name, and they answer differently. {{ua}} Firefox has a headless switch too. It was not installed on this machine, so you see the code and not a run. {{firefox}} Sometimes you need a window on a machine with no screen. A virtual display called Xvfb gives you one. {{xvfb}} Then the test that bites. It passes in the default mode, fails in the other headless mode, and passes again with a window. The cause is one line, and the fix is to delete it. {{bite}} Last, you time the same suite with a window and without, and read what the number says. {{speed}}
